title: HOMFLY polynomial approximation

problem.name: HOMFLY polynomial approximation
problem.statement_latex: Given a braid and fixed admissible root-of-unity parameters for a Hecke-algebra representation, estimate the normalized HOMFLY invariant of its trace closure within additive $\varepsilon$. The normalization is the representation's normalized Markov trace.
problem.statement_text: Given a braid and fixed admissible root-of-unity parameters for a Hecke-algebra representation, estimate the normalized HOMFLY invariant of its trace closure within additive $\varepsilon$. The normalization is the representation's normalized Markov trace.

hardware.description_latex: The one-clean-qubit model uses one initialized control qubit together with a polynomial-size maximally mixed register; coherent controlled representation gates and repeated measurements implement the estimator.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n,m,1/\varepsilon)$ gates by Jordan--Wocjan normalized-trace estimation in the one-clean-qubit model, for the representation families constructed in the paper.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n,m,1/\varepsilon)$ gates by Jordan–Wocjan normalized-trace estimation in the one-clean-qubit model, for the representation families constructed in the paper.

classical.headline_latex: Classical evaluation by Hecke-algebra state propagation is exponential in the representation size parameter. The Jones specialization contains the $\mathsf{DQC1}$-complete additive-approximation regime. For an implemented $q$-qubit, $g$-gate circuit over a fixed finite algebraic gate set, classical simulation also gives $\min\{O(g2^q),\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)},\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\}$. Here $w$ is a contraction width and $s$ is the size of the sparse bounded-fan-in Boolean encoding of scalar path counts at the required precision; gate synthesis and precision contribute to $g,s$.
